example.japanese: 彼は結局来ませんでした。
example.english: He didn't come in the end.

meaning: If A is 〇〇, then B is also

example.japanese: 犬も走れば猫も走る。
example.english: If the dog runs, then the cat runs too.

meaning: As A happens, B happens as well

example.japanese: 人は年を取るにつれて賢くなります。
example.english: As people age, they become wiser.

example.japanese: 本を読むたびに、新しいことを学びます。
example.english: Every time I read a book, I learn something new.

example.japanese: 例えば、りんごやオレンジなどの果物が好きです。
example.english: For example, I like fruits such as apples and oranges.

meaning: Speaking of; when it comes to

example.japanese: 日本といえば、桜が有名ですね。
example.english: Speaking of Japan, cherry blossoms are famous, right?

example.japanese: この本はあの本よりも面白いです。
example.english: This book is more interesting than that book.

meaning: It looks like; it seems like

example.japanese: 彼は眠いように見える。
example.english: He looks sleepy.

meaning: It would be nice if 〇〇; should..

example.japanese: どこへ行けばいいですか。
example.english: Where should I go?

meaning: Difficult to 〇〇; hard to 〇〇

example.japanese: 信じ難いことですが、彼は本当に優しいです。
example.english: It's hard to believe, but he is really kind.

meaning: To be scheduled or expected to

example.japanese: 明日、会議があることになっています。
example.english: A meeting is scheduled for tomorrow.

meaning: To get used to; to become accustomed to.

example.japanese: 新しい学校に慣れました。
example.english: I got used to the new school.

meaning: There is no other way; it can't be helped

example.japanese: もう雨が降っているから、仕方がない。
example.english: It is already raining, so it can't be helped.

meaning: It is not the time for doing something

example.japanese: 遊んでいる場合じゃない。
example.english: It is not the time to be playing.

example.japanese: ついケーキを食べた。
example.english: I accidentally ate the cake.

meaning: Cannot due to circumstances; must not

example.japanese: 行くわけにはいかない。
example.english: I cannot go (due to circumstances).

meaning: I feel that; I have a feeling that

example.japanese: 今日は雨が降りそうな気がする。
example.english: I have a feeling it will rain today.

meaning: It's not impossible; there is a possibility

example.japanese: 学校へ行けないことはない。
example.english: It's not impossible to go to school.

example.japanese: 勉強するつもりで、図書館に行きました。
example.english: I went to the library intending to study.

example.japanese: 別に忙しくない。
example.english: I'm not particularly busy.

meaning: Not only ... but also; as well as

example.japanese: 彼女は日本語だけでなく英語も話せます。
example.english: She can speak not only Japanese but also English.

example.japanese: いくらべんきょうしても、わかりません。
example.english: No matter how much I study, I do not understand.

meaning: Not ever; never by any means

example.japanese: 私は決してあきらめません。
example.english: I will never give up.

example.japanese: 彼は、お金がないながらも、幸せです。
example.english: Although he has no money, he is happy.

example.japanese: 彼は歴史に関する本を書いています。
example.english: He is writing a book related to history.

meaning: Depending on; by means of; because of.

example.japanese: この本は学生によって書かれました。
example.english: This book was written by a student.

example.japanese: メールを通じて知らせます。
example.english: I will inform you through email.

meaning: Taking the trouble to; specially; expressly

example.japanese: わざわざ来てくれてありがとう。
example.english: Thank you for coming all the way here.

meaning: If only...; it would have been....

example.japanese: 行けばよかったのに。
example.english: If only I had gone...

example.japanese: 彼は学生ばかりでなく、先生でもあります。
example.english: He is not only a student, but also a teacher.

example.japanese: もしかしたら明日雨が降るかもしれない。
example.english: Perhaps it might rain tomorrow.

example.japanese: ケーキなんか食べたい。
example.english: I want to eat something like cake.

example.japanese: 私は水さえあれば生きられます。
example.english: I can live with just water.

example.japanese: この薬を飲みさえすれば、元気になります。
example.english: If only you take this medicine, you'll get better.

example.japanese: 雨が降ったって、遊びに行きます。
example.english: Even if it rains, I will go out to play.

example.japanese: 学校に行く途中で犬を見ました。
example.english: I saw a dog on my way to school.

example.japanese: 彼は医者として働いています。
example.english: He is working as a doctor.

example.japanese: その本はとても読めない。
example.english: It's impossible to read that book.

example.japanese: もしも雨が降ったら、外に行きません。
example.english: If it rains, I won't go outside.

meaning: In accordance with, as X happens, Y happens

example.japanese: 温度が上がるにしたがって、虫が多くなる。
example.english: As the temperature rises, the number of insects increases.

meaning: There is no choice but to 〇〇; have to 〇〇

example.japanese: お金がないから、行くしかない。
example.english: There's no money, so I have no choice but to go.

example.japanese: あなたはコーヒーが好きですか、それとも紅茶が好きですか？
example.english: Do you like coffee, or do you like tea?

meaning: It doesn’t matter if; it’s okay to

example.japanese: 雨が降ってもかまわない。
example.english: It doesn’t matter if it rains.

example.japanese: 熱いうちに食べてください。
example.english: Please eat it while it's hot.

meaning: After doing something; as a result of.

example.japanese: 日本に行った上で、ガイドをしました。
example.english: After going to Japan, I did the guided tour.

example.japanese: どんなに勉強しても、試験は難しいです。
example.english: No matter how much I study, the exam is difficult.

example.japanese: ふと思い出した。
example.english: I suddenly remembered.

meaning: What on earth; what the heck

example.japanese: 一体何が起こったのですか。
example.english: What on earth happened?

example.japanese: こんなに美しい花なんて！
example.english: What a beautiful flower!

example.japanese: たくさん食べたせいで、おなかが痛いです。
example.english: Because I ate a lot, I have a stomachache.

example.japanese: 遅れたのは事故だったものだから。
example.english: I was late because there was an accident.

example.japanese: 確かにこの本は面白いです。
example.english: Certainly, this book is interesting.

example.japanese: たとえ雨が降っても、私は行きます。
example.english: Even if it rains, I will go.

example.japanese: 彼はそれをわざとしました。
example.english: He did it on purpose.

example.japanese: これはあまり辛くないです。
example.english: This is not too spicy.

example.japanese: 子供向けの本です。
example.english: This is a book intended for children.

example.japanese: あれを食べるべきではない。
example.english: You should not eat that.

example.japanese: 日本に一度も行ったことがありません。
example.english: I have never been to Japan, not even once.

example.japanese: 天気予報に反して、今日は晴れました。
example.english: Contrary to the weather forecast, it was sunny today.

example.japanese: 学校において勉強します。
example.english: I study at school.

example.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は雨です。
example.english: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

meaning: With all (e.g., one's love, heart, feelings)

example.japanese: 愛を込めて手紙を書きました。
example.english: I wrote the letter with all my love.

example.japanese: ドアを開けた途端、猫が逃げた。
example.english: Just as I opened the door, the cat ran away.

example.japanese: 学校というのは、勉強するところです。
example.english: School means a place to study.

example.japanese: 彼は帰ろうとしない。
example.english: He does not try to go home.

example.japanese: 私はバスに乗る代わりに歩きます。
example.english: I walk instead of taking the bus.

example.japanese: 先生のおかげで、合格できました。
example.english: Thanks to the teacher, I was able to pass.

example.japanese: 明日は休日です。すなわち、学校はありません。
example.english: Tomorrow is a holiday. That is, there is no school.

example.japanese: 父が帰るように、晩ご飯を作ります。
example.english: I will cook dinner so that dad can come back.

example.japanese: 工事中です。
example.english: It is under construction.

example.japanese: 一度にたくさんのお茶を飲みます。
example.english: I drink a lot of tea all at once.

meaning: For sure; emphasizes the preceding word

example.japanese: 今こそ、勉強しなければならない。
example.english: Now is the time to study, for sure.

meaning: That is to say; it means that.

example.japanese: 明日はテストだということだ。
example.english: It means that there is a test tomorrow.

meaning: The more A, the more B

example.japanese: 食べれば食べるほど、お腹がいっぱいになる。
example.english: The more you eat, the fuller you become.

example.japanese: りんごか何か食べたい。
example.english: I want to eat an apple or something.

meaning: Leaving something as it is; keep doing something

example.japanese: ドアを開けっぱなしにする。
example.english: To leave the door open.

example.japanese: 彼は先生というより友達だ。
example.english: He is more like a friend than a teacher.

example.japanese: 東京は桜で有名です。
example.english: Tokyo is famous for cherry blossoms.

meaning: By all means; No matter what

example.japanese: どうしても日本に行きたい。
example.english: I want to go to Japan no matter what.

meaning: Is not; am not; are not

example.japanese: 私は学生じゃない。
example.english: I am not a student.

meaning: Used when trying to recall something

example.japanese: 明日は誕生日だっけ。
example.english: Is tomorrow your birthday?

example.japanese: 夏が好きなことから、この国に住むことにした。
example.english: From the fact that I like summer, I decided to live in this country.

example.japanese: 雨が降りました。そのために、試合が中止になりました。
example.english: It rained. For that reason, the match was canceled.

meaning: There is no way to; Cannot be done.

example.japanese: この問題はむずかしくてわかりようがない。
example.english: This problem is difficult and there is no way to understand it.

meaning: Cannot help but feel or do

example.japanese: 犬を見たら、笑わずにはいられない。
example.english: When I see a dog, I can't help but smile.

distractors: てしまう or ちゃう

example.japanese: ケーキはここにいくらでもあります。
example.english: There are as many cakes as you like here.

example.japanese: 今日、学校を休みます。なぜなら、病気だからです。
example.english: Today, I will be absent from school because I am sick.

example.japanese: 私にかわって、彼が行きます。
example.english: He will go instead of me.

meaning: Used to; reminiscing about past habits

example.japanese: 子供のころ、よく公園で遊んだものだ。
example.english: When I was a child, I used to often play in the park.

meaning: Only after; for the first time after

example.japanese: 外に出てはじめて、雨が降っていることに気づいた。
example.english: Only after going outside did I realize it was raining.

meaning: Even if done, it won't help

example.japanese: 泣いても始まらない。
example.english: Even if you cry, it won't help.

example.japanese: 子供別として、みんな行きました。
example.english: Apart from the children, everyone went.

example.japanese: ドアを開けようとする。
example.english: Try to open the door.

meaning: to the extent of; as much as

example.japanese: 今日の天気は信じられないほど良い。
example.english: Today's weather is unbelievably good.

example.japanese: 猫は犬ほど速くない。
example.english: Cats are not as fast as dogs.

example.japanese: この問題はなかなか難しいです。
example.english: This problem is quite difficult.

example.japanese: 東京から大阪にかけて雨です。
example.english: It is raining from Tokyo to Osaka.

example.japanese: 日本語を勉強している最中に電話が鳴りました。
example.english: While I was studying Japanese, the phone rang.

meaning: It seems that; appears to be

example.japanese: 雨が降ったとみえる。
example.english: It seems that it rained.

meaning: Just as; in the same way as

example.japanese: 本を読むとおりに書いてください。
example.english: Please write just as you read the book.

meaning: Not necessarily so; not always true.

example.japanese: すべての猫が好きとは限らない。
example.english: Not everyone likes cats.

example.japanese: 私は友達に本を借りてあげました。
example.english: I borrowed a book for my friend.

example.japanese: ところで、明日の天気はどうですか？
example.english: By the way, how is the weather for tomorrow?

example.japanese: りんごやバナナなどを食べます。
example.english: I eat apples, bananas, etc.

example.japanese: 彼は学生に違いない。
example.english: There is no doubt that he is a student.

meaning: It ends with; it’s resolved by.

example.japanese: 本を読んで済む。
example.english: It is resolved by reading a book.

meaning: It would be fine if; it’d be good if...

example.japanese: しけんにうかるといいです。
example.english: It would be nice if I pass the exam.

example.japanese: ついに雨がやみました。
example.english: The rain finally stopped.

example.japanese: 食べれば食べるほど、おいしく感じる。
example.english: The more I eat, the more delicious it feels.

example.japanese: 入り口が多い一方だ。
example.english: There are many entrances on one hand.

example.japanese: 昨日、8時間ぐらい寝ました。
example.english: I slept for about 8 hours yesterday.

example.japanese: 日本には行ったことがありますか？
example.english: Have you ever been to Japan?

example.japanese: 子どもでさえできる。
example.english: Even a child can do it.

meaning: (Although) I say; Even if one says...

example.japanese: 昨日は海に行ったと言っても、近くの川でした。
example.english: Although I say I went to the sea yesterday, it was actually a nearby river.

meaning: It does not mean that; it's not the case that

example.japanese: 彼が遅いわけではない。
example.english: It’s not that he is late.

example.japanese: 食べるばかりで、遊びません。
example.english: He only eats and doesn't play.

example.japanese: 今日は雨だけど、明日は晴れです。
example.english: It's raining today, but it will be sunny tomorrow.

example.japanese: 彼はまるでロボットのようだ。
example.english: He is just like a robot.

distractors: そうに or そうな

example.japanese: 今年は去年に比べて暑いです。
example.english: This year is hotter compared to last year.

example.japanese: 私はりんごを食べました。さらにバナナも食べました。
example.english: I ate an apple. Furthermore, I also ate a banana.

meaning: For a moment; for a while

example.japanese: しばらく、お待ちください。
example.english: Please wait for a moment.

meaning: While you’re at it; taking the opportunity

example.japanese: スーパーに行くついでに、パンを買いました。
example.english: While I was at the supermarket, I bought bread.

example.japanese: 勉強すべきです。
example.english: You should study.

example.japanese: 急ぐことはない。
example.english: There is no need to hurry.

example.japanese: この本は面白くない。むしろ、つまらない。
example.english: This book is not interesting. Rather, it's boring.

example.japanese: 学生に対して、先生は宿題を出します。
example.english: The teacher gives homework to the students.

example.japanese: 日本の文化について話します。
example.english: I will talk about Japanese culture.

example.japanese: 彼は男っぽいです。
example.english: He is manly.

meaning: It would have been better if...

example.japanese: 映画を見ればよかった。
example.english: It would have been better if I had watched the movie.

meaning: To go through; to finish completely

example.japanese: 彼は本を読み切った。
example.english: He finished reading the book.

example.japanese: 本を直す。
example.english: Fix the book.

example.japanese: すでに朝ごはんを食べました。
example.english: I have already eaten breakfast.

meaning: Try to; give it a try (commanding)

example.japanese: これを食べてごらん。
example.english: Try eating this.

meaning: Even if you do, it's useless

example.japanese: 勉強してもしょうがない。
example.english: Even if you study, it's useless.

meaning: Together with; as X happens, Y also happens.

example.japanese: 花がさくと共に、天気も良くなる。
example.english: As the flowers bloom, the weather also becomes good.

example.japanese: 彼はたくさん勉強した。結果、試験に合格した。
example.english: He studied a lot. As a result, he passed the exam.

example.japanese: あなたは学生のくせに勉強しない。
example.english: Even though you are a student, you don't study.

example.japanese: 明日、雨が降るんだって。
example.english: I heard that it will rain tomorrow.

example.japanese: 焼きたてのパンを食べます。
example.english: I eat freshly baked bread.

example.japanese: 雨だから、外に行けないのはしょうがない。
example.english: Since it’s raining, it can’t be helped that we can’t go outside.

example.japanese: ドアを開けて通す
example.english: Open the door and let (someone/something) through.

example.japanese: 朝から夜にかけて働きます。
example.english: I work from morning to night.

example.japanese: まさか、あの人が先生！？
example.english: No way, is that person a teacher!?

meaning: For; concerning; as far as... is concerned.

example.japanese: 私にとって、日本語はとても大切です。
example.english: For me, Japanese is very important.

example.japanese: せいぜい三ヶ月ぐらい日本にいます。
example.english: I will stay in Japan for at most three months.

example.japanese: あまりにも暑いです。
example.english: It is too hot.

example.japanese: 毎日ごとに勉強します。
example.english: I study every day.

example.japanese: 一人きりです。
example.english: It's just one person.

example.japanese: 勉強しないと合格できない。
example.english: If I don't study, I cannot pass.

example.japanese: なるべくはやく来てください。
example.english: Please come as quickly as possible.

example.japanese: 日本といえば、寿司ですね。
example.english: Speaking of Japan, it's sushi, right?

meaning: In other words; that is to say

example.japanese: 彼は学生です。つまり、テストを受けます。
example.english: He is a student. In other words, he takes tests.

example.japanese: 彼の仕事ぶりはすごいです。
example.english: His way of working is amazing.

example.japanese: この本は長くて、一日で読み切れない。
example.english: This book is long, and I can't finish reading it in one day.

meaning: To be crowded; to be packed

example.japanese: 電車が込みます。
example.english: The train gets crowded.

example.japanese: この本は子供向きです。
example.english: This book is suitable for children.

example.japanese: 図書館では静かにしないといけないから。
example.english: Because you must be quiet in the library.

example.japanese: 今日は晴れだと思った。ところが、雨が降り始めた。
example.english: I thought it would be sunny today. However, it started raining.

example.japanese: もちろん、いきますよ。
example.english: Of course, I will go.

example.japanese: こどものへやはおもちゃだらけです。
example.english: The child's room is full of toys.

example.japanese: 日本語を勉強することが好きです。
example.english: I like studying Japanese.

example.japanese: 私はめったに映画を見ない。
example.english: I rarely watch movies.

example.japanese: 雨が降るにしても、私は行きます。
example.english: Even if it rains, I will go.

meaning: On the occasion of; at the time of

example.japanese: 図書館を利用する際に、カードが必要です。
example.english: When using the library, a card is necessary.

example.japanese: さて、お茶を飲みましょう。
example.english: Well then, let's drink some tea.

example.japanese: この本は読めそうもない。
example.english: It doesn't look like I can read this book.

distractors: そうに or そうな

meaning: For the sake of; in order to

example.japanese: 勉強するために本を読みます。
example.english: I read books in order to study.

example.japanese: 宿題をしてからでないと遊べません。
example.english: You cannot play unless you finish your homework first.

example.japanese: 科学的な本
example.english: A scientific book

example.japanese: 昨日、勉強するつもりだった。
example.english: I was intending to study yesterday.

example.japanese: このケーキは安い割においしいです。
example.english: This cake is delicious considering how cheap it is.

example.japanese: 勉強せずに出かけました。
example.english: I went out without studying.

meaning: to fit; to match; to come together

example.japanese: 彼らは意見が合う。
example.english: Their opinions match.

example.japanese: 私は水だけ飲みます。
example.english: I only drink water.

example.japanese: 本を読みかける。
example.english: (I) start reading a book.

example.japanese: この プロジェクトは 学生 を中心に 進めます。
example.english: This project will be carried out centered around students.

example.japanese: 学校をはじめ、図書館や公園も行きました。
example.english: Starting with the school, I also went to the library and the park.

example.japanese: 彼はテレビを見てばかりいる。
example.english: He does nothing but watch TV.

meaning: On top of that; in addition to

example.japanese: 今日は雨が降っている上に、風も強いです。
example.english: On top of raining today, the wind is also strong.

example.japanese: 食べることは食べたが、おいしくない。
example.english: The fact is, I ate, but it wasn't tasty.

meaning: Would; is it the case that...

example.japanese: 天気はいいのでしょうか。
example.english: Would the weather be good?

example.japanese: こんなに難しい問題がわかるわけがない。
example.english: There is no way I can understand such a difficult problem.

meaning: To pretend; to act as if

example.japanese: 彼は寝ているふりをする。
example.english: He pretends to be sleeping.

example.japanese: 彼は忘れがちです。
example.english: He tends to forget.

example.japanese: 風邪気味です。
example.english: I feel a bit like I have a cold.
